package_info.package_manager: Linux (malware distributed as shell scripts, binaries, and Perl scripts)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware campaign, not a versioned package)
package_info.why_malicious: The campaign delivers multiple malicious payloads including a downloader, cryptocurrency miner (XMRig), and DDoS IRC bot. It uses brute-force SSH attacks for initial access, then downloads and executes additional malware, abuses system resources for illicit mining, and establishes C2 communication for further control and DDoS attacks.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful SSH brute-force, the script downloads a tar archive containing the XMRig miner from a remote server, extracts it, sets execute permissions, and launches the miner.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of binaries from untrusted remote sources is a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal post-authentication scripts do not fetch and execute remote binaries, especially cryptocurrency miners.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment scripts in DevOps may download and install software, but only from trusted sources and with user awareness.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the XMRig binary is executed with a configuration file, hijacking system CPU resources to mine Monero and sending mining results to a remote mining pool.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited cryptocurrency mining is a hallmark of resource hijacking malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not mine cryptocurrency without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Mining software is legitimate when installed knowingly by the system owner.
key_indicators: Presence of xmrig binary in non-standard locations
Mining configuration files (config.json) in /tmp or hidden directories
High CPU usage by unknown processes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Perl script connects to an IRC server, joins a channel, and awaits DDoS commands, enabling remote attackers to launch DDoS attacks from the compromised host.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated IRC bot connections and DDoS command execution are classic signs of botnet malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Perl scripts do not connect to IRC servers and await remote attack commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IRC bots may be used for legitimate chat automation, but not for DDoS or malware control.

attack_chain.action: Brute-force SSH credentials to gain unauthorized access to Linux servers.
Deploy and execute downloader shell script to fetch additional payloads from remote servers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of miner and bot binaries

attack_chain.action: Extract and execute XMRig miner to hijack system resources for cryptocurrency mining.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing illicit mining and resource abuse

attack_chain.action: Deploy and execute Perl DDoS IRC bot to connect to attacker-controlled IRC channels for remote command and control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Botnet participation and DDoS attack capability

behavioral_signatures: Automated download and execution of binaries from remote, non-standard URLs
Presence and execution of XMRig miner in /tmp or hidden directories
Outbound IRC connections from non-user processes
High CPU usage by unknown or suspicious processes
network_indicators: Downloads from hxxp://172.105.211.21/, hxxp://167.172.103.111/, hxxp://172.104.170.240/, hxxp://wget.hostname.help/, hxxp://pateu.freevar.com/
Outbound IRC traffic to attacker-controlled servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized SSH logins followed by the download and execution of binaries from suspicious external URLs. Detect the presence of XMRig or similar mining binaries in temporary or hidden directories, and watch for configuration files (config.json) associated with mining. Alert on outbound IRC connections from servers, especially if initiated by Perl scripts or unknown processes. Correlate high CPU usage with the presence of these indicators to identify illicit mining activity.
